The Entire Thesis in One Real-Life Story (30 Seconds)

Imagine you manage a tomato farmer cooperative (FPO) in Madhya Pradesh. It is 6:00 a.m. You open the government's AGMARKNET website on your phone. Your local mandi paid ₹1,500 per quintal yesterday, while another mandi 200 km away listed ₹2,000 per quintal yesterday.

That looks like an easy +₹500/qtl profit! So you load a truck and send it. What goes wrong? When the truck arrives, three real-world traps hit: (1) truck freight, yard fees, and heat decay eat into the spread; (2) yesterday's ₹2,000 spike crashes back down in a volatile market; or (3) worst of all, the destination mandi has no auction running for your crop that day (a "silent/blank" arrival board), forcing an expensive turn-back. Our study proves that chasing tempting online spreads loses money nearly half the time (45.07%) — and shows how 9-choice zero-tuned-weight pocket-calculator rules capture ~98.8% of full-season 17-month ML Mean and ~94% of conditional tail protection at n_train = 0 before you call the destination trader on the phone.

What This Tool ACTUALLY Is

  • An upstream 6 a.m. call-priority alert filter (PhoneCall_TopK_Open: 4.99% loss, cond_ES10 −₹355.07 vs B2 −₹691.79) ahead of live trader dialing.
  • Built strictly on ≤ t−1 public quotes across 171 zero-lookahead markets (2025–2026) AND 166 clean markets over 2018–2023 (383,952 trips) conditioned on 2024 corridor inclusion (reverse-survivorship: 481/647 historical markets excluded).
  • Verified inside shared dispatches (CommonIntersection_DS_cap_DB, n=33,398): +₹65.66 Mean & +₹53.40 ES10 pure routing lift.

What This Tool Does NOT Claim

  • Does NOT replace calling a trader (arhtiya) before loading a truck, nor claim 0-parameter beats full-season ML (17m Mean-Q10 edges Mean & tail at n_train=113,374).
  • Does NOT measure actual farmer cash receipts (under Outsider_MinPrice_LCV_4pctArh, Safe_EV Mean compresses to ₹102.62 vs B2 ₹33.86).
  • Does NOT guarantee exact OSRM coordinates everywhere: 56/171 markets collide on legacy parent coordinates (35.23% exact coverage, N=6,605 still holds p=0.001).

2. Why Naive Online Spreads Fail: The Four Hidden Traps

  1. Reporting Lag (Yesterday's Price ≠ Today's Price): At 6 a.m., today's auction hasn't happened yet. Many smaller mandis upload prices 1 to 7 days late. Yesterday's high price is often an outdated spike that already dropped.
  2. Physical Frictions (Freight + Stylized Fees + Transit Decay):
    • Road Freight (F): Base loading ₹35 + ₹0.45 per road km (×1.45 in Himachal Pradesh, where 91.59% of roads are single-lane hill roads; LCV + 4% arhtiya stress also tested).
    • Stylized State Fee Tiers: 0.5% to 1.5% charged on destination sale value (0% inside the same district or if unsold), anchored qualitatively to state APMC deregulation status (PIB 154554) and stress-tested from 0% to 6% commission.
    • Transit Decay: Modeled operationally from NABCONS (2022) marketing-level crop loss shares (Tomato 3.25%, Onion 1.96%, Apple 1.64%, Potato 0.86%), stress-tested under repaired _spoil_return_leg S6 (full 24τ+hrs+24w + ERA5: Safe_EV Mean ₹307.39, ES10 −₹576.57, cond_ES10 −₹725.73).
  3. Silent / Blank Arrival Boards (28.67% of Naive Trips!): On 28.67% of naive spread-chasing trips, the destination market uploads no trade at all for that crop on arrival day. Under sequential arrival rules (you don't know tomorrow's prices in advance!), a truck facing a blank yard turns back instead of gambling blindly.
  4. Sunday / Weekly Holiday Blindness & Price Swings: A mandi closed every Sunday still looks "75% active" in a 28-day average — fooling average-based filters on weekends. Meanwhile, high-variance markets (like Apple and Tomato) swing violently between yesterday and arrival day.

3. The Honest Candidate C Breakthrough: 9-Choice Cold-Start, 2×2 Split & 17m ML/CQR

Earlier drafts concluded that ML and conformal models failed because initial models suffered from 5-month off-season training starvation (Ridge, HGBR_RiskAverse, and unnormalized OR_Vargas_MeanVar_g0002 at cond_ES10 −₹511.42) and a homoscedastic Split-CQR bug (0 switches). Once fixed in Revision v8: (a) heteroscedastic Split-CQR re-ranks destinations (8,848 switches in 5m: MG_T1..T4_Intact_matched 66.32%, Mean ₹356.78, ES10 −₹323.41, cond_ES10 −₹414.44; 8,115 switches in 17m: ML_17m_CQR80_valmatch 57.30%, Mean ₹364.03, cond_ES10 −₹367.09); and (b) full-season 17m GBDTs (n_train_17m = 113,374) reach Mean ₹455.83, ES10 −₹320.02, cond_ES10 −₹420.57 (ML_17m_MeanQ10_Hybrid_eq63; ablating safe_ev_feat in NoSafeEV_eq63 hits ₹458.27 / −₹423.88 autonomously!), while OR_Stylized_MeanSD_17m_valmatch hits ₹443.57 / −₹439.77. Why keep the 9-choice calculator rule? With zero tuned weights and zero training data (n_train = 0), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 captures ~98.8% of MeanQ10 Mean and ~94% of cond_ES10 tail protection on day 1!

Rule 1: Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (9 Fixed Choices, 0 Tuned Weights) & 2×2 Orthogonal Decomposition

pdow · G1SD − Froad  ≡  pdow(G1SD − Froad) + (1 − pdow)(−1.0 Froad)  >  0

Plain English + Exact Identity: G1SD subtracts 1-SD recent swing (cv28) and stylized fee from yesterday's price; pdow is 8-week same-weekday reliability. The identity proves it prices −1.0 F sunk freight on silent days (Safe_EV_Phys_m0 uses −1.5 F). 2×2 Orthogonal Split: Ortho_Pure_cv28_only (71.91% disp, Mean ₹421.62, ES10 −₹387.46, cond_ES10 −₹447.13) drives ~100% of tail truncation, whereas Ortho_Pure_pdow_only (84.10% disp, Mean ₹466.68, cond_ES10 −₹607.18) drives diversion avoidance and Mean lift!

HP Scale Non-Invariance Fix (ScaleInv_Safe_EV_24tau): When F/G1SD < 0.10 (79.52% of HP apple trips), omitting proportional spoilage breaks pdow. Adding 24τ spoilage + 1.5F cuts HP apple ep_loss from 27.91% → 17.92% (ES10 −₹958.08, cond_ES10 −₹1,616.08 vs −₹2,003.68; Safe_EV_Sunk_pFloor50 hits 15.17%).

Rule 2: RT_2F_Min_m0 (Class-8 4-Function Phone Calculator — Omits Volatility cv28)

pmin × G  >  2 × Froad     (equivalently:   G / (2 Froad)  >  1 / pmin)

Plain English: Uses plain fee-adjusted spread G and stricter reliability pmin = min(rep28, pdow) against round-trip freight 2F. Because it omits cv28, it keeps high Mean (₹463.98) yet misses conditional tail truncation (cond_ES10 −₹618.35) and fails under ≤ t−2 latency (p = 0.981).

10-Second Phone Calculator Example (Real Numbers!)

Route: 200 km MP Tomato trip. Local = ₹1,500, dest = ₹2,000, fee = 1.5%, freight F = 35 + 0.45 × 200 = ₹125, swing cv28 = 15% → G = +₹470/qtl, G1SD = +₹174.50/qtl.

  • Case A — Reliable Weekday Mandi (pdow = 0.90, pmin = 0.85): Safe_EV: 0.90(174.50−125)+0.10(−125) = +₹32.05 > 0 → DISPATCH! | RT_2F: 0.85 × 470 = ₹399.50 > ₹250 → DISPATCH!
  • Case B — Sunday-Closed Mandi (pdow = 0.20, pmin = 0.20): Road baseline B2 sees 470 − 125 = +₹345 and goes blindly! Safe_EV gives 0.20 × 174.50 − 125 = −₹90.10; RT_2F gives 0.20 × 470 − 250 = −₹156.00 → STAY HOME!

Key verified takeaways: On clean 166-mkt 2018–2023 (N = 383,952, reverse-survivorship 481/647 excluded), Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 wins ES10 (+₹169.27) and cond_ES10 (+₹155.08; +₹174.27 vs equal-dispatch B2_eq_SafeM0) in 6/6 years (p = 0.001; 2020/2023 Means NS). 5. The 10 Most Relevant Research Papers (Your Literature Map in Plain English)

Your thesis connects four classic research areas. Memorize these 10 foundational literature anchors — each is explained in two plain-English sentences so you can cite them naturally in any viva or review response:

PILLAR 1 • Agricultural Spatial Arbitrage & Why Price Portals Alone Fail
Paper & VenueCore Idea in Plain EnglishHow MandiGuard Connects / Differs
1. Baulch (1997)
Am. J. Agric. Econ. (AJAE)		 Introduced the Parity Bounds Model: two markets are only profitably connected if their price gap exceeds real transfer costs (freight + fees + risk). Our economic foundation — we translate parity bounds from ex-post macro tests into an ex-ante 6 a.m. truck dispatch filter.
2. Jensen (2007)
Quarterly J. Economics (QJE)		 Classic Kerala fishermen study: mobile phones let fishermen call coastal markets in real time, eliminating waste and raising profits dramatically. Explains why live phone calls (PhoneCall_TopK_Open) remain vital — MandiGuard prioritizes alerts before dialing arhtiyas.
3. Fafchamps & Minten (2012)
World Bank Econ. Rev.		 Large field RCT in Maharashtra sending daily SMS mandi prices to farmers found almost zero average income gain because transport and execution frictions blocked arbitrage. Directly proves why raw AGMARKNET screens mislead (our 45.07% naive loss rate) — raw prices need reliability and volatility filtering.
4. Mitra et al. (2018)
Rev. Econ. & Statistics		 Field experiment with West Bengal potato farmers showing middlemen, transport barriers, and asymmetric information absorb raw price spreads. Reinforces why we stress-test Outsider_Mid/MinPrice_LCV_4pctArh (compressing Mean to ₹102.62) and never claim modeled cash receipts.
5. Levi et al. (2020; 2025)
PNAS & Manuf. Serv. Oper. Manag. (MSOM)		 Evaluated Karnataka's Unified Market Platform (e-auctions), showing digital platforms raise realized farmer prices when auction execution is reliable and transparent. Shows the institutional complement: reliable execution platforms solve the arrival uncertainty our filter guards against today.
PILLAR 2 • Indian Mandi Forecasting, Missing Data & Farmer Workflows
Paper & VenueCore Idea in Plain EnglishHow MandiGuard Connects / Differs
6. Madaan et al. (2019) & Ma et al. (2019)
ACM COMPASS & ICTD		 Built time-series and matrix-completion ML models on AGMARKNET to forecast prices and fill in missing daily quotes, optimizing RMSE (average prediction error). Key Research Gap: Predicting prices accurately does not protect against a truck arriving at a blank yard or losing big on volatile days.
7. Ziegler et al. (2019)
ACM ICTD		 Field user study with Indian vegetable farmers showing market tools only get adopted if they are ultra-simple and fit morning trader-calling habits. Motivates our 9-choice cold-start calculator (Safe_EV_Sunk_m0) that captures ~98.8% of 17m ML Mean with zero training history.
PILLAR 3 • Decision-Focused Learning, Heuristics & Risk-Aware Abstention
Paper & VenueCore Idea in Plain EnglishHow MandiGuard Connects / Differs
8. Chow (1970) & El-Yaniv & Wiener (2010)
IEEE TIT & JMLR		 Founded selective prediction (reject option): when mistakes are far costlier than staying silent, abstaining cuts catastrophic risk dramatically. Theoretical root of staying home at ₹0; CommonIntersection_DS_cap_DB proves we also add +₹65.66 Mean / +₹53.40 ES10 routing lift.
9. Elmachtoub & Grigas (2022) & Mandi et al. (2024)
Manage. Sci. & JAIR 80		 Introduced Smart "Predict, Then Optimize" (SPO) and surveyed Decision-Focused Learning (DFL) benchmarks across 80+ combinatorial settings (mandi2024dfl). Frames our 17m Mean-Q10 GBDT frontier (autonomously reaching ₹458.27 / −₹423.88 without safe_ev_feat) alongside 0-data Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (DeMiguel 2009; Vargas 2026 Mean-SD ₹443.57 / −₹439.77).
PILLAR 4 • Missing-Data Bounds & Worst-Case Tail Risk (ES10)
Paper & VenueCore Idea in Plain EnglishHow MandiGuard Connects / Differs
10. Manski (1990) & Rockafellar & Uryasev (2000)
AER & Journal of Risk		 Manski introduced nonparametric bounds under non-ignorable missingness; Rockafellar & Uryasev formalized coherent Expected Shortfall / CVaR (worst 10% average). Anchors exact fractional ES10/cond_ES10, 25.45% Open-MAR break-even, and exact coupled Manski cond_ES10 (Supp1 +₹152.20, Supp2 +₹105.96).

6. Radical Honesty: Every Negative Result & Boundary You MUST Know

Why Knowing Your Own Weaknesses Wins Every Viva & Review

Examiners love catching students hiding negative results — and immediately respect students who state exact failure boundaries clearly. Memorize these five honest disclosures:

  1. Missing-Quote Bounds (Open-MAR Reversal & Coupled Manski cond_ES10): Under 100% Open-MAR, road baseline B2 earns +₹97.01/qtl higher Mean (₹698.17 vs ₹601.16; break-even 25.45% or +₹348.61/qtl; 26.65% ERA5), while coupled Manski cond_ES10 remains positive on Supp1 (+₹152.20) and Supp2 (+₹105.96).
  2. When Mean Gains Vanish (Free Turn-Back & Hindsight): Under free return (div = 0), Mean (+₹12.03 / +₹11.21, p = 0.22–0.26) is NS while ES10 keeps +₹174.40 / +₹169.82. Under 3-day hindsight, B2 leads Mean (₹549.81 vs ₹533.14), while Safe_EV cuts ES10 (−₹279.93 vs −₹588.34).
  3. Subgroup, UP Atom & Reverse-Survivorship Limits: HP (B = 12) fails cond_ES10 (p = 0.1239) and studentized checks (p = 0.1879, pcgm,gstar = 0.2995); Apple is borderline (cond_ES10 p = 0.0550); UP has an unconditional q10 = 0 atom (7.28% < 10% loss rate); Potato trails RR by −₹17.20; 166-mkt 2018–2023 is reverse-survivorship conditioned on 2024 (481/647 excluded; 2020/2023 Means NS); and 56/171 legacy geocodes collide (35.23% exact coverage, N=6,605 p=0.001).
  4. HP Scale Non-Invariance & Honest 17m ML Frontier: On HP apples (N = 2,802), F/G1SD < 0.10 on 79.52% breaks pdow (41.38% cond loss, cond_ES10 p = 0.0940 NS); ScaleInv_Safe_EV_24tau cuts ep_loss 27.91% → 17.92% (cond_ES10 −₹1,616.08; pFloor50 15.17%). On full 17m (ntrain = 113,374), MeanQ10 reaches ₹455.83 / −₹420.57 (NoSafeEV ₹458.27 / −₹423.88) and Split-CQR hits cond_ES10 −₹367.09 (8,115 switches), though zero formal conformal coverage guarantees are claimed.
  5. Outsider Bargaining, SUTVA Crowding & Blocked Gate J: Outsider_MinPrice_LCV_4pctArh compresses Safe_EV Mean to ₹102.62 (34.29% loss), SUTVA 10% crowding drops Mean to −₹5.31 (needs k ≤ 2 coordination), and prospective field validation (Gate J) remains open.

7. Quick Viva Survival Guide: 6 Toughest Examiner Questions & 15-Second Answers

Q1: "How does your 9-choice calculator rule compare against properly trained ML and Split-CQR?"
Answer: "Earlier 5m off-season starvation and homoscedastic CQR (0 switches) masked ML's potential. Trained on 17 full seasonal months (n_train = 113,374), ML_17m_MeanQ10_Hybrid_eq63 hits ₹455.83 / cond_ES10 −₹420.57 (NoSafeEV hits ₹458.27 / −₹423.88 autonomously) and heteroscedastic Split-CQR reaches cond_ES10 −₹367.09 (8,115 switches). Yet Safe_EV_Sunk_m0 (n_train = 0) captures ~98.8% of that Mean and ~94% of conditional tail protection with zero historical training data and pocket-calculator transparency."
Q2: "Isn't this post-hoc to 2025–2026, and how do small clusters (B=12) and 2018–2023 hold up?"
Answer: "We label 2025–2026 explicitly as specification-locked exploratory inference (PREREG_A18 pholm,2s = 0.0040; CGM pcgm,gstar = 0.00511 / 0.01001 for H_A18_1, 0.04887 / 0.06800 for H_A18_2; 1-way pwild,webb6,1w = 0.0005), and disclose HP B=12 non-significance and UP's unconditional q10=0 atom. Frozen rules also transfer to clean 166 markets over 2018–2023 (N = 383,952, 6/6 yrs ES10 & cond_ES10, 2020/2023 Means NS), conditioned transparently on 2024 corridor inclusion (481/647 excluded)."
Q3: "What drives Safe_EV's gain — volatility, reliability, routing, or just abstaining? What about trader calls?"
Answer: "Our 2×2 orthogonal decomposition proves Ortho_Pure_cv28_only (cond_ES10 −₹447.13) supplies ~100% of tail truncation while Ortho_Pure_pdow_only (Mean ₹466.68, −₹607.18) supplies diversion avoidance and Mean lift. Inside shared dispatches (CommonIntersection_DS_cap_DB, n = 33,398), Safe_EV also adds +₹65.66 Mean and +₹53.40 ES10 purely from better routing. Before loading, PhoneCall_TopK_Open still cuts losses to 4.99% (cond_ES10 −₹355.07 vs B2 −₹691.79)."
Q4: "What if blank AGMARKNET rows were open yards, or return legs suffer full heat decay?"
Answer: "B2 only passes Safe_EV on Mean if ≥ 25.45% of silent yards clear at full lagged prices (Open-MAR gives B2 +₹97.01/qtl Mean), yet exact coupled Manski cond_ES10 stays positive through Supp1 (+₹152.20) and Supp2 (+₹105.96). Under repaired _spoil_return_leg S6 (full 24τ+hrs+24w + ERA5), Safe_EV earns ₹307.39 / −₹576.57 / −₹725.73, and keeps +₹366.85 cond_ES10 under Stoch_CondMAR_p1.00."
Q5: "What breaks on Himachal graded apples and real-world geocodes / outsider pricing?"
Answer: "On HP apples (N=2,802), F/G1SD < 0.10 on 79.52% breaks the pdow screen (scale non-invariance); ScaleInv_Safe_EV_24tau solves this by cutting ep_loss 27.91% → 17.92% (cond_ES10 −₹1,616.08). On geocodes, 56/171 markets collided, leaving 35.23% exact coverage (N=6,605 still passes ES10 p=0.001). On Outsider_MinPrice_LCV_4pctArh, Safe_EV Mean drops to ₹102.62 (vs B2 ₹33.86)."
Q6: "What is your single next step to turn this into a top-tier journal paper?"
Answer: "A one-season FPO field pilot logging 200–500 real 6 a.m. arhtiya confirmation calls, truck bills, and auction patti slips — directly measuring the true silent-open rate against our 25.45% break-even threshold while rebuilding corridors with our repaired sub-yard-first geocoder (Gate J)."
